lookback_source.quote: Check all nutritional approaches performed after admission/entry or reentry to the facility and within the 7-day look-back period.

lookback_notes: The assessor's observation window for the resident-status columns is the 7-day look-back period (Column 2: performed prior to admission/entry or reentry and within the 7-day look-back period; Column 3: performed after admission/entry or reentry and within the 7-day look-back period). The item form additionally states Column 2 is "the last 7 days" and Column 3 is "the last 7 days." Two other, different windows are stated for the SNF PPS Stay columns: Column 1 is days 1 through 3 of the SNF PPS Stay starting with A2400B, and Column 4 is the last 3 days of the SNF PPS Stay ending on A2400C. The pages do not state whether Column 2 is applicable to row C.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code K0520C for a mechanically altered diet, i.e., a diet that requires a change in texture of food or liquids (e.g., pureed food, thickened liquids).

source.quote: K0520C, mechanically altered diet – require change in texture of food or liquids (e.g., pureed food, thickened liquids).

federal_coding_rules.rule: A mechanically altered diet is a diet specifically prepared to alter the texture or consistency of food to facilitate oral intake (e.g., soft solids, puréed foods, ground meat, thickened liquids); it should not automatically be considered a therapeutic diet.

source.quote: A diet specifically prepared to alter the texture or consistency of food to facilitate oral intake. Examples include soft solids, puréed foods, ground meat, and thickened liquids. A mechanically altered diet should not automatically be considered a therapeutic diet.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not capture a trial of a mechanically altered diet (e.g., pureed food, thickened liquids) during the observation period in K0520C.

source.quote: Assessors should not capture a trial of a mechanically altered diet (e.g., pureed food, thickened liquids) during the observation period in K0520C, mechanically altered diet.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Enteral feeding formulas should not be coded as a mechanically altered diet.

source.quote: Enteral feeding formulas: — Should not be coded as a mechanically altered diet.

federal_coding_rules.rule: A documented mechanical soft diet with honey-thick liquids required in the last 7 days and continuing at discharge is coded in K0520C for the While a Resident and At Discharge columns (example: K0520C3 and K0520C4 checked).

federal_coding_rules.rule: A resident who was on a mechanical soft diet only during the acute hospital stay and was upgraded to a regular texture diet prior to hospital discharge, and who had a regular diet for the entire nursing home stay, is coded K0520Z (none of the above) rather than K0520C for the While a Resident and At Discharge columns.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The pages do not tie K0520C to any payment or case-mix classification. The only payment-related statements in the K0520 section are that Column 1 and Column 4 assessment periods are defined by the first/last 3 days of the SNF PPS Stay, and that on the Interim Payment Assessment (IPA) the completion of K0520A, K0520B, and K0520Z (not K0520C) is required.

conflicts.topic: Coexisting observation windows for K0520 columns (7-day look-back vs. 3-day SNF PPS Stay windows)

positions.claim: Columns 2 and 3 use a 7-day look-back period (before/after admission, entry or reentry).

source.quote: Check all nutritional approaches performed after admission/entry or reentry to the facility and within the 7-day look-back period.

positions.claim: Columns 1 and 4 use 3-day windows tied to the SNF PPS Stay rather than the 7-day look-back.

source.quote: Check all nutritional approaches performed during the first 3 days of the SNF PPS Stay.

conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the document itself: the windows are column-specific — Columns 2 and 3 use the 7-day look-back, Column 1 uses days 1–3 of the SNF PPS Stay, and Column 4 uses the last 3 days of the SNF PPS Stay (p. K-11, p. K-12).
